industry: Precious metals (cash-for-gold/scrap buyers, pawn, coin & bullion dealers, precious-metals IRA / physical metals sellers)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Guaranteed returns', 'can't lose', 'safer than the bank', or 'government-backed' metals investments (FINRA/CFTC Lies vs Facts; FTC Act s.5)
'Highest price guaranteed' / 'top dollar' (GOLD-precious-metals-001/002/005) without a clear, testable comparison basis — and never if you will not honor it (16 CFR 239)

'Up to 98.5% of market price' (GOLD-precious-metals-006) unless that percentage is actually paid for the stated purity/weight for a meaningful share of transactions, and 'market price' is defined (spot vs melt vs dealer bid)
Fake official look: U.S. Mint, Treasury, IRS, Social Security, or eagle/seal styling that implies federal endorsement (39 USC 3001(h); 31 USC 333 Mint name/emblem misuse)
'Numismatic' / 'semi-numismatic' premiums used to justify huge markups on common coins (FINRA/CFTC investor bulletin)
'Free gold' / big freebies that hide the spread and commissions (FINRA Q7 red flag)
IRA claims that skip custodian identity, storage location, all fees, and IRC 408(m) eligibility limits
Implying the IRA custodian vetted the dealer or the investment (SEC/FINRA/NASAA SDIRA alert: custodians typically do not)
Age-targeted 'protect your retirement' scare copy as a default audience claim without client-specific evidence (fraudsters target retirees; that is not a license to stereotype every buyer)
compliance_notes: FTC Act s.5: investment and buyback claims must be truthful and substantiated before mailing. No guaranteed profits; disclose material risks.
16 CFR Part 23 (Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Guides): do not misrepresent metallic content, karat/fineness, weight, or value in ads or appraisals.

FINRA + CFTC Investor Bulletin (2024-03-20) and CFTC 'Lies Versus Facts' flier: warn against cold calls, unsolicited email, junk mail, and pop-up dealers for physical metals/IRA pitches; demand written fees, spread vs spot, buy-back price, and registration checks. Free-kit lead magnets followed by high-pressure phone closings are a known scam pattern — legal only if fully non-deceptive, and still a compliance red zone.
SEC/FINRA/NASAA Investor Alert on self-directed IRAs: custodians generally do not investigate the assets or promoters; precious metals in SDIRAs carry fraud, fee, and liquidity risks.

IRC 408(m): most collectibles are treated as distributions; exceptions exist for certain coins and for gold/silver/platinum/palladium bullion of required fineness held by a bank or approved nonbank trustee. Home storage of IRA metals can be treated as a taxable distribution. Ads must not imply any metal/coin is IRA-eligible.

39 USC 3001(h): government look-alike solicitations are nonmailable unless truly affiliated or the required conspicuous disclaimers appear on the mailpiece and outer cover ('THIS IS NOT A GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT' / federal-endorsement disclaimer).
31 USC 333 / U.S. Mint business guidelines: civil fines for misuse of Mint or Treasury names, emblems, or symbols implying sponsorship.

FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule (16 CFR 435): if selling metals by mail/phone/online, have a reasonable basis to ship in the advertised time (or 30 days), and offer delay consent or refund.

FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule (16 CFR 310): investment telemarketing (including some inbound responses to ads) requires cost/fee disclosures before payment; honor entity-specific Do Not Call; National DNC applies to outbound telemarketing. Precious-metals investment cases have alleged TSR violations.

State/local secondhand precious-metals dealer and pawn licenses, hold periods, ID/reporting, and sometimes cash-payment limits vary (e.g., Maryland state licensing + hold; Connecticut restrictions). Show license numbers where required. Temporary buying events often need separate local permits.
Pawn loans: state pawn statutes and Truth in Lending/Reg Z may apply to credit terms; do not advertise 'loan' APRs without required disclosures.
Spot vs dealer spread honesty: always selling above spot and buying below is normal — hiding the spread is the fraud pattern FINRA flags.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear of inflation/collapse is allowed when non-deceptive; joy/relief on cash-for-gold is equally valid.
Only laws/compliance are hard limits — and they are heavy in this vertical.
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Never quote agency/gold response numbers as fact; label agency-only unverified.
No retiree/senior demographic default without industry-specific evidence.

emotion_by_offer.evidence_strength: strong compliance evidence; thin positive response evidence (not in gold set)

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold-set 'HIGHEST PRICE GUARANTEED' / 'top dollar' (GOLD-precious-metals-001/002/005) vs FTC substantiation and 16 CFR 239 guarantee rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: drop absolute 'highest' claims unless a clear, honest comparison basis is stated and honored; prefer 'free estimate' + transparent bid.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Market-common free IRA kit + telemarketing vs FINRA/CFTC warning not to respond to junk mail/cold calls and vs TSR disclosure duties
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: if a client insists on kits, require full written fee/spread/custodian disclosure on the mailer path, no fake official design, no guaranteed returns, and lawful DNC/TSR practices. Prefer local bullion transparency over boiler-room lead gen.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Fraudsters target retirees (FINRA/CFTC) vs Patrick's ban on unsupported age/demographic angles
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick + evidence rule wins for creative targeting: do not default to 'senior gold' audiences. You may factually warn about scams in compliance copy; you may not invent 'retirees buy gold' as the buyer thesis.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: 'Up to 98.5% of market price' (GOLD-precious-metals-006) vs spread honesty
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: define market price (spot/melt/dealer bid), purity gates, and typical payout; 'up to' needs a meaningful share actually receiving the max.
